svg.title: The Workers' Comp Mod-Control Team
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-comp-mod-control-team; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: The Workers' Comp Mod-Control Team; subtitle: Who owns claims, reserves, class codes, and return-to-work; caption: Practitioners say the most common mistake is that no one monitors claims experience, and some experts believe 60 to 70 percent of mods are wrong.; assumptions note: Role names are structural groupings of practitioner tips. The 60 to 70 percent figure is a belief Gordon Coyle attributes to some experts, not a measured rate.; note: Sources are Gordon Coyle of The Coyle Group, Ryan Hanigan of JJ Doorhy & Associates, ClinardInsGroup, and WorkCompConsultants.; center: role: Claims Monitoring Owner; headcount: One named owner; focus: Gets the last five years of loss runs explained line by line and verifies every open reserve before loss figures go to NCCI, since reserves count the same as paid dollars.; spokes: role: Broker Advocate; type: External advisor; kpi: Runs tools estimating the mod without one shock loss when a mod above 1.0 threatens bid eligibility with a general contractor.; role: Dedicated Work Comp Carrier; type: Carrier with in-house nurses and caseworkers; kpi: Pushes injured workers back sooner, shifting more of each loss to the frequency side.; role: Class Code and Mod Auditor; type: Consultant; kpi: Completes class code review and checks subcontractor certificates for excluded owners and clerical-only coverage before the auditor does.; role: Light-Duty Coordinator; type: Internal program; kpi: Places workers in doctor-approved light duty, including nonprofit partner placements that keep indemnity dollars off loss runs and out of the mod.
